blocks.text: Urinary (kidney) stones are hard, crystalline mineral materials that stick together into small pebbles in the kidney or urinary tract. They may stay in the kidneys or travel out through the urinary tract.

blocks.caption: Kinds of kidney stone
rows: hypercalciuria (high calcium in urine) and hyperoxaluria (high oxalate in urine)
hyperuricemia (high uric acid in the blood)

blocks.text: Continued dehydration raises the chance of stones forming. Doctors can judge the kind of stone from a urine test: acidic urine suggests calcium oxalate, alkaline urine calcium phosphate, and persistently acidic urine uric acid.

items: Extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy (ECSWL): an instrument called a lithotripter generates shockwaves from outside the patient's body; they break the stone into small pieces, most of which pass out in the urine.

Percutaneous nephrolithotripsy (PNL), for larger stones: a tube is inserted from the patient's back into the kidney, a small camera (nephroscope) is passed through it to see the stone, ultrasound equipment breaks the stone, and the pieces are grasped and pulled out.

blocks.alt: A patient sits against a support while a lithotripter outside the body sends shockwaves towards the kidney. Two enlarged circles show the kidney: in the first, shockwaves reach a stone in the renal pelvis; in the second, the stone has broken into smaller pieces.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.5: Extracorporeal shockwave lithotripsy (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.5).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Lithotripter, Shockwaves (at the body and in the first enlargement), Stones, Smaller pieces of stones.

blocks.alt: A section through the back with a kidney. A tube passes from outside through the skin into the renal pelvis; a stone lies where the ureter begins. A flexible line joins the tube to a nephroscope outside the body.
blocks.caption: Figure 14.6: Percutaneous Nephrolithotripsy (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 14.6).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Renal pelvis, Stone, Skin, Tube, Nephroscope.
